rules.title: Truth in Renting Act - Distribution Requirement
rules.quote: Every landlord subject to the Truth in Renting Act, (N.J.S.A. 46:8-43 to 51), hereinafter the Act, is required to distribute one copy of the Truth in Renting Statement to each of their tenants within 30 days after it has been posted by the Department on its website and shall thereafter provide a copy of the most current statement to each new tenant at or prior to the time the tenant executes a lease for the rental unit.
rules.summary: Landlords must distribute the Truth in Renting Statement to tenants within 30 days after it is posted on the Department website and provide it to new tenants at or before lease execution.
rules.coverage_text: The Act calls for distribution of the statement by the landlord to all tenants with a rental term of at least one month living in residences with more than two dwelling units, or more than three if the landlord occupies one of the units.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to hotels, motels, or other guest houses serving transient or seasonal tenants, or to owner-occupied buildings of three or fewer units

rules.title: Good Cause Requirement for Lease Non-Renewal
rules.quote: No landlord of residential rental properties except those in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.summary: Landlords of most residential rental properties must have good cause to refuse to renew a lease, whether written or oral.
rules.coverage_text: No landlord of residential rental properties except those in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to owner-occupied two or three family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units

rules.title: Lease Termination Due to Domestic Violence
rules.quote: victims of domestic violence may terminate their lease without penalty prior to the expiration of the lease by providing the landlord with a written notice that the tenant or a child of the tenant faces an imminent threat of serious physical harm from a specific person, (that must be identified in the written notice), if the tenant remains on the premises
rules.summary: Victims of domestic violence may terminate their lease without penalty by providing written notice that the tenant or child faces an imminent threat of serious physical harm if they remain on the premises, along with required documentation.

related_citations.evidence: Has a certified copy of a permanent restraining order issued by a court under the Prevention of Domestic Violence Act of 1991 (N.J.S.A. 2C:25-17 et seq.)

rules.coverage_text: This law does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals

rules.title: Security Deposit Return for Domestic Violence Lease Termination
rules.quote: If a tenant terminates the lease agreement prior to the expiration of the lease pursuant to the Safe Housing Act, (N.J.S.A. 46:8-9.6), the tenant is entitled to the return of their security deposit. Within 15 business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant's security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant's agent.
rules.summary: If a tenant terminates their lease under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest within 15 business days after the lease is terminated.

related_citations.evidence: pursuant to the Safe Housing Act, (N.J.S.A. 46:8-9.6)

The landlord may charge the tenant for any money due the landlord under the terms of the lease, including damages to the property that are not ordinary wear and tear and any rent due and owing at the time the lease is terminated (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19)

rules.title: Lease Termination Due to Disabling Illness, Accident or Death
rules.quote: under the Lease Termination Due to Disabling Illness, Accident or Death Law, a tenant may break their lease, under certain conditions. A 40-day written notice of lease termination is required in each instance. The tenant must vacate and return possession of the property to the landlord at least five working days prior to the 40th day following the landlord's receipt of the notice to terminate.
rules.summary: Tenants may break their lease under certain conditions including disabling illness or accident by providing 40-day written notice and vacating at least five working days before the 40th day.
rules.exemption_note: Applies to tenants suffering disabling illness/accident, tenants 62+ accepted into assisted living/nursing home/continuing care, tenants 62+ accepted into low-/moderate-income housing, or upon death of tenant or spouse

rules.title: Service Members Civil Relief Act - Lease Termination
rules.quote: a service member leasing an apartment before entering the military has the legal right under this act to terminate the lease under the following circumstances: At any time after the renter's entry into military service; or The service member, while in military service, executes the lease and thereafter receives military orders for a permanent change of station outside of the continental United States or to deploy with a military unit for a period of not less than 90 days.
rules.summary: Service members may terminate their lease after entering military service or upon receiving military orders for a permanent change of station outside the continental U.S. or deployment for at least 90 days.

related_citations.evidence: The landlord is required to return the security deposit in accordance with the applicable Security Deposit Law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26).

rules.title: No Discrimination Against Service or Guide Dogs
rules.quote: The Law Against Discrimination as set forth in N.J.S.A. 10:5-29.2, prohibits discrimination against handicapped, blind, or deaf people in renting or leasing housing accommodations. A handicapped, blind, or deaf person who has a service or guide dog, or who obtains a service or guide dog, shall have full and equal access to all housing accommodations and shall not be required to pay extra compensation. Any lease or rental agreement prohibiting pets shall not apply to a service or guide dog owned by a handicapped, blind, or deaf tenant.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot discriminate against handicapped, blind, or deaf tenants who have service or guide dogs, and no-pet lease provisions do not apply to service or guide dogs.

rules.title: Pets in Senior Citizen Housing Projects
rules.quote: The Pets in Housing Projects law, N.J.S.A. 2A:42-103, et seq., defines 'senior citizen housing project,' as any building or structure having three or more rental dwelling units. It does not apply to owner-occupied premises that do not have more than three rental dwelling units, or any health care facility. Any senior citizen residing in a senior citizen housing project and providing written notice to the landlord is allowed to own or care for a pet.
rules.summary: Senior citizens residing in housing projects with three or more rental units are allowed to own or care for a pet after providing written notice to the landlord.
rules.coverage_text: any building or structure having three or more rental dwelling units. It does not apply to owner-occupied premises that do not have more than three rental dwelling units, or any health care facility.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to owner-occupied premises with three or fewer units or health care facilities

rules.title: Maximum Security Deposit
rules.quote: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month's rent
rules.summary: Landlords cannot collect a security deposit that exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.coverage_text: The Security Deposit Law applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests in writing that the Security Deposit Law apply (30 days after request).

rules.title: Interest on Security Deposits
rules.quote: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing on the renewal or anniversary of the tenant's lease or on January 31, if the tenant has been given written notice, that the interest payments will be paid on January 31 of each year
rules.summary: Interest earned on a security deposit must be paid to the tenant annually on the lease anniversary date or on January 31 if notice is given.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to seasonal use or rental (term of not more than 125 consecutive days for residential purposes by a person having a permanent place of residence elsewhere).

rules.title: Return of Security Deposit
rules.quote: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.summary: Landlords must return the security deposit plus interest, less any deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.penalty: If a landlord fails to return the security deposit within 30 days, the tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

rules.title: Security Deposit Penalty for Willful Withholding from Government-Assisted Tenants
rules.quote: Any landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or on behalf of a tenant who has received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance, may be penalized. The landlord may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.
rules.summary: Landlords who willfully withhold a security deposit from a tenant receiving government assistance face a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense.

related_citations.evidence: The penalty shall be collected and enforced by summary proceedings pursuant to the Penalty Enforcement Law (N.J.S.A. 2A:58-12).

rules.coverage_text: Applies to tenants who have received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance.
rules.penalty: $500 to $2,000 civil penalty per offense, collected by summary proceeding pursuant to Penalty Enforcement Law.

rules.title: Source of Income Anti-Discrimination
rules.quote: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.summary: It is illegal for landlords or rental agencies to discriminate in renting based on source of lawful income, among other protected characteristics.
rules.coverage_text: The law applies to all landlord-tenant relationships, except those involving two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex, i.e. YMCA and age-restricted housing, as it pertains to familial status.
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions for owner-occupied two-family dwellings, rooms in owner or resident-occupied single home, and single-sex residences (with respect to familial status).
rules.penalty: Landlords who violate this law are subject to substantial fines and penalties, up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)).

rules.title: Proper Notice for Rent Increase Eviction
rules.quote: This law provides that before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
rules.summary: Before evicting a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, the landlord must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Exemption from Local Rent Control
rules.quote: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.summary: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: Exemption from local rent control for 30 years following completion of construction for newly constructed multiple dwellings.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – Good Cause Required for Eviction
rules.quote: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.
rules.summary: A landlord may only evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease if the landlord has good cause and can prove it in court.

related_citations.evidence: The Anti-Eviction Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12, was created to protect blameless tenants from eviction and was adopted in recognition of the housing shortage in the State.

rules.title: Notice to Quit Required for Good Cause Evictions (Except Nonpayment)
rules.quote: A 'Notice to Quit' is required for all good cause evictions, except for an eviction for nonpayment of rent (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2). A 'Notice to Quit' is a notice given by the landlord terminating the tenancy and ordering the tenant to vacate the premises.
rules.summary: For all good cause evictions other than nonpayment of rent, the landlord must serve a Notice to Quit on the tenant before filing an eviction suit.

rules.title: Landlord Registration Required to Evict
rules.quote: The landlord registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not been properly registered (N.J.S.A. 46:8-27 to -37).
rules.summary: A landlord cannot evict a tenant if the landlord has not properly registered the rental property as required by law.
rules.coverage_text: A landlord who owns a one or two-family non-owner-occupied home is required by law to file a registration statement with the clerk of the municipality in which the building is located. If the building has three (3) or more units, the statement must be filed with the Bureau of Housing Inspection
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two-family homes are not required to be registered.
rules.penalty: The maximum penalty is $500.00 for each offense, recoverable by a summary proceeding under 'The Penalty Enforcement Law' (N.J.S.A 2A:58-1 et seq.).

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Just Cause Requirement
rules.quote: The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes.
rules.summary: The Anti-Eviction Act requires just cause for eviction in most residential rental properties in New Jersey.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes. Does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant (with exceptions for occupants with no alternate residence).
rules.exemption_note: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units. Does not apply to hotel/motel/guest house transient or seasonal tenants (except occupants with no alternate residence). Does not apply to a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member who permanently occupies it.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Failure to Pay Rent
rules.quote: If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may immediately take legal action to have the tenant evicted. The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. If the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing a 14-day notice must be given before filing a suite for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict for nonpayment of rent without prior notice, except tenants in federally subsidized housing who must receive 14-day notice.
rules.exemption_note: Tenant may not be evicted if unpaid rent was used to continue utility services after landlord failed to pay.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Disorderly Conduct
rules.quote: If after given written Notice to Cease disorderly conduct, the tenant continues the disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict for continued disorderly conduct that destroys the peace after written Notice to Cease and at least three days Notice to Quit.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Damage or Destruction to Property
rules.quote: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict if a tenant has intentionally or through gross negligence caused destruction, damage, or injury to the property, with at least three days Notice to Quit.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Violation of Rules and Regulations
rules.quote: If after given a written Notice to Cease violating or breaching reasonable rules and regulations contained in the lease or accepted in writing by the tenant, the tenant continues to substantially violate or breach the rules and regulations, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction. In addition, any notices must be given on or before the start of a new month.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict for continued substantial violation of reasonable rules and regulations after Notice to Cease, with at least one month Notice to Quit given on or before the start of a new month.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Violation of Lease Covenants (General)
rules.quote: If the tenant continues to substantially violate or breach the reasonable covenants or agreements contained in the lease, after given written Notice to Cease violating or breaching those covenants or agreements and if the landlord has reserved a right of re-entry in the lease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for this type of eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict for continued substantial violation of lease covenants after Notice to Cease, if the lease reserves a right of re-entry, with at least one month Notice to Quit.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Failure to Pay Rent Increase
rules.quote: If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict for failure to pay a rent increase that is not unconscionable and complies with rent control and other laws, with at least one month Notice to Quit.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Health and Safety Violations or Removal from Rental Market
rules.quote: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction. The tenant can't be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.summary: Tenants may be evicted for health and safety violations, illegal occupancy correction, or governmental redevelopment with at least three months Notice to Quit and relocation assistance provided before eviction.
rules.key_value: 3 months; 6 times monthly rent for illegal occupancy

related_citations.evidence: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant's monthly rent.
The tenant may file a lien statement with the county clerk or registrar in order to enforce the lien (N.J.A.C. 5:11-8.5(c)).

rules.exemption_note: Tenants evicted for illegal occupancy receive relocation assistance equal to six times monthly rent from landlord; if unpaid, 18% annual interest accrues and amount becomes a lien on property.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Permanent Retirement from Residential Use
rules.quote: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict to permanently retire a building from residential use with at least 18 months Notice to Quit and no action until the lease expires.
rules.penalty: If landlord allows any residential use during five-year period after tenant vacates, landlord liable for three times damages plus attorney fees and costs, and civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Refusal to Accept Lease Changes
rules.quote: When the lease expires, the landlord may propose reasonable but substantial changes to the terms and conditions of the lease. If after written notice the tenant refuses to accept those changes the landlord may file a suit for eviction and the court will determine if the proposed changes are reasonable.
rules.summary: When a lease expires, landlords may evict if the tenant refuses to accept reasonable substantial changes to lease terms after written notice, with at least one month Notice to Quit.
rules.exemption_note: Landlord has burden of proof that changes are reasonable and do not substantially reduce tenant rights for tenants with protected tenancy status under Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act or Tenant Protection Act of 1992.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Habitual Late Rent Payment
rules.quote: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict tenants who continuously fail to pay rent or habitually pay late after written Notice to Cease, with at least one month Notice to Quit.
rules.exemption_note: Courts have ruled habitual late payments means more than one late payment following Notice to Cease. Landlord must continue giving reasonable notice when accepting late payments or original Notice to Cease may be waived.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Conversion to Condominium/Cooperative
rules.quote: If the landlord or owner of a building or mobile home park is converting the property from the rental market to a condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of two or more dwelling units or park sites, except as hereinafter provided in subsection (L) below, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict to convert property to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership with at least three years Notice to Quit and no action until lease expires.
rules.exemption_note: Up to five one-year stays of eviction granted if tenant not offered reasonable opportunity to examine comparable housing. Not more than one-year stay if landlord allows five months' free rent. No action against senior or disabled protected tenancy status tenants while protected.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Tenancy After Conversion - Owner Personal Occupancy
rules.quote: The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of three or less condominium or cooperative units seeks to evict a tenant whose initial tenancy began, by rental, after the master deed or agreement establishing the cooperative was recorded, because the owner seeks to personally occupy the unit, or has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who seeks to personally occupy it and the contract for sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.summary: Owners of three or fewer condominium or cooperative units may evict a tenant for personal occupancy or sale to buyer for personal occupancy with at least two months Notice to Quit and no action until lease expires.
rules.exemption_note: Applies only to tenants whose initial tenancy began after master deed or cooperative agreement was recorded.
rules.penalty: If landlord does not occupy unit for at least six months after tenant vacates, landlord liable for three times damages plus attorney fees and costs.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Employment-Based Tenancy
rules.quote: If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three days prior to filing a suit for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict tenants whose tenancy is based on employment with the landlord when that employment is terminated, with at least three days Notice to Quit.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Drug Conviction
rules.quote: The landlord may file a suit for eviction, if the tenant, including juveniles who have been found by the Court to be delinquent, has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to drug offenses that took place on the property, and has not in connection with his sentence either (1) successfully completed or (2) been admitted to and continues during probation participation toward completion of a drug rehabilitation program. Also, if the tenant lets a person who has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to drug offenses, occupy the premises for residential purposes whether it is continuously or occasionally, the landlord may file for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict tenants convicted of drug offenses on the property who have not completed drug rehabilitation, or who harbor such persons, with at least three days Notice to Quit within two years of conviction, delinquency finding, or release from incarceration.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to tenant allowing juvenile to reside who was found delinquent for drug use or possession. No suit may be brought more than two years after juvenile delinquency, conviction, or release from incarceration, whichever is later.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Conviction of Assault or Threats
rules.quote: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, or if a juvenile has been found by the court to be delinquent due to an offense involving assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, a member of the landlord's family or an employee of the landlord. Also, if the tenant permits a person he knows has been convicted of or has pleaded guilty to these offenses to reside at the premises continuously or occasionally, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict tenants convicted of assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, landlord's family, or employees, or who harbor such persons, with at least three days Notice to Quit within two years of conviction, delinquency finding, or release from incarceration.
rules.exemption_note: No suit may be brought more than two years after juvenile delinquency, conviction, or release from incarceration, whichever is later.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Civil Liability for Criminal Activities
rules.quote: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant is found by a civil court proceeding (not criminal) to be liable for involvement in theft of property located on the premises, involvement in assaults or terrorist threats against the landlord, a member of the landlord's family or an employee of the landlord, or involved in illegal drug activities that takes place on the premises and that tenant has not in connection with his sentence for the drug offense either (1) successfully completed or (2) been admitted to and continues during probation participation towards completion of a drug rehabilitation program.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict tenants found civilly liable for theft, assault, threats, or drug activities on the property who have not completed drug rehabilitation, or who harbor such persons, with at least three days Notice to Quit within two years.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to tenant allowing juvenile to reside who was found delinquent for drug use or possession. No suit may be brought more than two years after juvenile delinquency, conviction, or release from incarceration, whichever is later.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Conviction for Theft
rules.quote: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, or if a juvenile has been found to be delinquent by the Court due to an offense involving theft of property from the landlord or from tenants residing in the same building or complex. Also, if the tenant permits a person he knows has been convicted of or has pleaded guilty to these actions to reside at the premises continuously or occasionally, the landlord may file for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict tenants convicted of theft of property from the landlord or other tenants, or who harbor such persons, with at least three days Notice to Quit.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Human Trafficking
rules.quote: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant in a civil action is found to have committed a violation of the human trafficking provisions set forth in section 1 of P.L. 2005, c.77 (2C:13-8) within or upon the leased premises, building, or complex of the building and land appurtenant thereto, or the mobile home park, in which those premises are located, or, being the tenant or lessee of such leased premises, knowingly harbors or harbored a person engaged in human trafficking, or permits or permitted such a person to occupy those premises for residential purposes, whether continuously or intermittently. No action for removal pursuant to this subsection may be brought more than two years after the alleged violation has terminated.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict tenants found in a civil action to have committed human trafficking on the property or who harbor such persons, within two years after the violation has terminated.

related_citations.evidence: violation of the human trafficking provisions set forth in section 1 of P.L. 2005, c.77 (2C:13-8)

rules.exemption_note: No action may be brought more than two years after the alleged violation has terminated.

rules.title: Owner-Occupied Dwellings: Just Cause Eviction
rules.quote: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction. However, in these cases, the landlord must prove that the tenant (a) is staying after the expiration of the term of the lease, (b) is staying after a failure to pay rent, (c) is disorderly so as to destroy the peace and quiet of other tenants, (d) willfully destroys or damages the premises, (e) constantly violates the written rules and regulations or (f) violates any lease provision where the lease reserves a right of re-entry for such violations.
rules.summary: In landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings, tenants can only be evicted by court order for specific causes including lease expiration, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, property damage, rule violations, or lease violations where re-entry is reserved.
rules.key_value: 3 months for at-will/year-to-year; 1 month for month-to-month
rules.exemption_note: Notice requirements: three-month notice to quit for at-will or year-to-year tenancy; one-month notice for month-to-month tenancy. Three-day written Notice to Quit required for disorderly, destructive, or rule/lease violations. No notice required for nonpayment of rent.

rules.title: Rooming and Boarding Houses: Just Cause Eviction
rules.quote: The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau.
rules.summary: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good cause and notice requirements of the Anti-Eviction Act when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards.

related_citations.evidence: Any building having at least two (2) living units occupied by persons unrelated to each other without private kitchens and bathrooms is a rooming or boarding house if it does not meet one (1) of the exceptions in the Rooming and Boarding House Act (N.J.S.A. 55:13B-3).
There is a further requirement that the owner give at least three (3) working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting the eviction action for any resident (N.J.A.C. 5:26-3.4(c)).

rules.coverage_text: Buildings having at least two living units occupied by persons unrelated to each other without private kitchens and bathrooms, with certain exceptions (hotels with >85% temporary occupancy, school/college dormitories, buildings housing only college students, certain residences for the disabled).
rules.exemption_note: Owner must give at least three working days' notice to County Welfare Board before starting eviction action for any resident.

rules.title: Anti-Retaliation Protection
rules.quote: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot evict, substantially alter a lease, or refuse to renew a lease in retaliation for a tenant exercising their rights, including enforcing lease or legal rights, making good faith complaints to government authorities, or organizing tenant organizations.
rules.coverage_text: All rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings. Tenant must have notified landlord in writing and given reasonable time to correct violation before making complaint to government authority.
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue landlord for damages in a civil action.

rules.title: Self-Help Eviction Prohibition
rules.quote: Self-help eviction is entry into a dwelling unit and removal of tenants without their consent or without a judgment from a court, are not permitted in New Jersey under any circumstances. A landlord or any other person who enters an apartment or property without a court order authorizing such entry and/or holds a tenant's belongings unlawfully by force or threat of monies owed may be liable for damages to the tenant.
rules.summary: Self-help evictions, including entering a dwelling without court order, removing tenants without their consent or court judgment, or holding tenant belongings unlawfully, are prohibited and landlords may be liable for damages.

related_citations.evidence: the removal of a tenant's belongings from a premise by a landlord after the eviction may be done only in accordance with the Abandoned Property Law, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-72 to 84

rules.penalty: Court may award possession and all damages, including court costs and reasonable attorney fees. If dwelling cannot be returned, court may award damages. Landlord may be charged with disorderly conduct.

rules.title: Foreclosure Eviction Protections
rules.quote: Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90-day notice to quit when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence. However, if a tenant has a lease agreement that goes beyond the 90 days the landlord may not take action to evict the tenant until after the lease expires and the 90-day notice to quit has been given.
rules.summary: After foreclosure, tenants must receive 90-day notice to quit only if the buyer wants to personally occupy the property as primary residence; tenants with leases beyond 90 days cannot be evicted until lease expires and 90-day notice is given.

related_citations.evidence: In a residential property containing more than 10 dwelling units, the new owner must provide notice to tenants occupying the property by conspicuously displaying a copy of the "NOTICE TO TENANTS" in a prominent location (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-70(c)2).
Pursuant to the New Jersey Foreclosure Fairness Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-69 et seq.), pressure tactics include but are not limited to (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-71(b))

rules.coverage_text: All residential rental units, including month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units.
rules.exemption_note: New owner must provide notice to tenants within 10 business days after sale. Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. Acceptance of bona fide monetary offers to vacate must be voluntary and in writing with five-day review period; pressure tactics are prohibited.
